note: A contract may be CLOSED only when every proof below exists in the tree. scripts/contract-gate.sh enforces that: a claim with no test behind it is a claim, not a control.

contracts.invariant: Identical inputs produce byte-identical output, and the stored derivation re-derives from the file itself
contracts.measure: two consecutive builds over the fixture feed, byte comparison, then `dozor verify`

contracts.invariant: A released NORA loads the output and enforces it, with no NORA change
contracts.measure: run the published NORA image against a generated blocklist, assert 403 and that the reason string survives

contracts.invariant: An unreadable feed or an empty inventory never overwrites an existing blocklist
contracts.measure: missing feed -> exit 2, empty inventory -> exit 3 even when proactive rules could be written, previous file byte-identical afterwards

contracts.invariant: A version the matcher cannot decide is reported, never treated as safe
contracts.measure: an unparsable version in the inventory appears in x-dozor-unmatched and in no rule

contracts.invariant: An expired exception fails the build instead of renewing itself
contracts.measure: policy with expires in the past -> exit 4

contracts.invariant: A wholly-malicious package collapses to one `version: "*"` rule, and a partly-malicious one does not. A report whose ranges cover every version is the whole package, with or without a version list beside them
contracts.measure: fixture with both shapes; assert the rule set; an all-versions range with and without a list, and a list beside a bounded range

contracts.invariant: Advisories from another ecosystem never leak into the blocklist
contracts.measure: a PyPI advisory in the npm fixture produces no rule

contracts.invariant: Closed by default: a policy that sets nothing blocks every wholly-malicious package in the feed and every version a malicious report lists for a package in the inventory, cached or not. Blocking less is a line in the policy; the CLI flag can only ask for more
contracts.measure: held fixture (no malicious version has a copy): the default policy blocks the listed version and the whole packages, the lowered policy blocks none, --proactive adds the whole packages back, an exception still holds a listed version

contracts.invariant: A malicious report is never dropped for the length of its version list: the list is kept for a malicious report, and for any report without ranges
contracts.measure: a malicious report with 147 versions, with and without ranges, keeps all of them; a non-malicious one with ranges falls back to the ranges and is counted as skipped

contracts.invariant: A policy value or key Dozor does not know fails the build (exit 5), and the previous blocklist survives: a typo opens nothing
contracts.measure: malicious = "blcok", an unknown malicious_versions, a misspelt key, an unknown key in an exception -> load error / exit 5, previous file byte-identical

contracts.invariant: Peak RSS on the full npm feed stays under 100 MB
contracts.evidence: 2026-09-05: 173 MB peak, 24.9 MB retained index. The gap is transient build allocation, not data. Reserving capacity up front and streaming the output writer are the open items.

contracts.invariant: Scan-on-publish (a synchronous verdict on push) is out of scope
contracts.measure: n/a — would require a resident service with an in-memory index, which D-ADR-1 forbids
